newsitem.title: DENMARK: Natural gas giants see world demand booming.
newsitem.headline: Natural gas giants see world demand booming.

text.p: COPENHAGEN, June 13, Reuter - Executives of the world's leading natural gas companies said on Friday they saw global demand increasing even faster than previous bullish forecasts.

Burckhard Bergmann, vice chairman of Germany's largest gas conmpany Ruhrgas said that a demand increase in western Europe to some 415-435 billion cubic metres (bcm) a year by 2010 was a common view in the industry.
That compared with predictions three years ago of 350-375 bcm for the same period, he said.
"But what is really remarkable," he added, "is that gas marketing companies so quickly contracted additional gas to match the higher demand expectations.

"No less than 40 bcm a year were additionally contracted on a long term basis to cover the demand gap seen in 1994 and to satisfy the additional demand now anticipated," he told delegates on the last day of the huge World Gas Conference here,
Harald Norvik, president of Norway's Statoil, was even more bullish in his demand projection.

He said that Western European demand will reach 510 bcm a year by 2010, up from 350 bcm last year, and that demand in the whole of Europe, including Turkey, will leap from 419 bcm last year to 612 bcm in 2010.
Demand in Asia is also set to boom, Koshiro Goda, vice president of the Japan Gas Association told the conference.
He said demand in east Asia will more than double, to around 300 bcm by 2010 from a current 140 bcm.
Much of this will be met by liquefied natural gas (LNG) delivered by ship, but extra volumes will also be delivered by a new pipeline infrastructure.
This point was backed up by Rem Vyakhirev, chairman of Russia's largest company and the world's largest gas company Gazprom.
He said that Russia is looking to develop a new pipeline system in eastern Siberia early next century to deliver gas to China, North and South Korea, and "very likely" Japan.
